Title: What Your Urine Color Is Actually Telling You

Description:
About 80 to 90 percent of bladder cancer cases start with red urine that doesn't hurt at all - that's just one of several signals urine color can give you. Pale yellow means well hydrated, dark yellow or amber means you need more fluids, pink or red can mean a UTI, kidney stones, an enlarged prostate, or painless bladder cancer, and dark brown or tea-colored urine can point to a liver issue or rhabdomyolysis after an extreme workout.

A little extra darkness usually just means more water. Painless red urine is the one to get checked, and tea-colored urine with severe muscle pain needs urgent care too.
